Currently no check subcommand. Also need cmd_bump, cmd_check, cmd_compare functions as distinct entry points for subcommands. That likely means we should expose functions that can be called programmatically. For example, cmd_bump(bump_type, version) returns bumped string. cmd_compare(v1, v2) returns compare result. cmd_check(version) returns bool if valid.

Also need to adjust regex to semver.org spec. Let's review current regex. It seems close but maybe missing some parts. Official spec: major.minor.patch, optional pre-release preceded by '-', optional build preceded by '+'. Pre-release identifiers separated by '.'; each ident must be alphanumeric and hyphen, but cannot be empty, cannot have leading zeros for numeric identifiers? Official spec: numeric identifiers must not have leading zeros. Also must be 0 or non-zero digits. Build identifiers can be any alphanumeric or hyphen. The current regex is:

(?P<major>(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*))
\. 
(?P<minor>(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*))
\. 
(?P<patch>(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*))
(\-(?P<prerelease>
    (?:0|[1-9A-Za-z-][0-9A-Za-z-]*)
    (\.(?:0|[1-9A-Za-z-][0-9A-Za-z-]*))*
))?
(\+(?P<build>
    [0-9A-Za-z-]+
    (\.[0-9A-Za-z-]+)*
))?

This seems okay but may allow leading zeros in prerelease numeric parts? It uses (?:0|[1-9A-Za-z-][0-9A-Za-z-]*). That allows numeric identifiers like '01'? Actually [1-9A-Za-z-] first char can be digit 1-9 or letter or hyphen. But if numeric id '01', first char '0' would fail because pattern for numeric part: "0" or [1-9A-Za-z-][0-9A-Za-z-]*. For '01', first char '0' matches '0', but then the entire string '01' must match '0' OR [1-9A-Za-z-][0-9A-Za-z-]*. '0' only matches single '0', not '01', so fails. Good. But then numeric part '12' would match [1-9A-Za-z-][0-9A-Za-z-]*, first char '1', rest '2', ok. So leading zero numeric part disallowed. That matches spec.

But spec also forbids hyphen at start? I think hyphen allowed after first char. Eg pre-release 'alpha-1' allowed. The pattern includes hyphen in [1-9A-Za-z-], so hyphen can be first char of identifier, which may be disallowed? Actually spec: identifiers must consist of only ASCII alphanumerics and hyphens; numeric identifiers must not have leading zeros. Hyphen can be anywhere except leading zero? I think hyphen can be anywhere except numeric? Let's check official spec: "Identifiers MUST comprise only ASCII alphanumerics and hyphens [0-9A-Za-z-]. Identifiers MUST NOT be empty." No restriction on hyphen at start. So allowed.

Ok maybe regex fine.

But requirement R2: update regex to align with official spec. Might need to adjust to allow build as optional and prerelease.
